title: genai scorer timeout: Scorer.run bounds every scorer invocation with a daemon thread; None means 300s, 0 disables
answers: A custom scorer hangs and stalls my whole mlflow.genai.evaluate run. How do I bound one scorer call?
Why does a timed-out scorer show up as a SCORER_ERROR feedback instead of failing the evaluation?
How do I turn off the scorer timeout for one judge scorer, or set a per-scorer limit?
Where is the scorer timeout enforced for offline evaluate, session scorers and online monitoring?
Why did my test asserting the scorer thread name MlflowGenAIEvalScorer start failing?
body:
Path: Every scorer invocation (offline evaluate, session-level scorers, online monitoring, ensemble sub-scorers) goes through `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.run`; the `@scorer(timeout=...)` option (`scorer`) is stored on `Scorer.timeout`.
Rule: In `Scorer.run`, `timeout=None` resolves to `DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT` (300s) and `0` disables the bound; a positive value goes to `Scorer._run_with_timeout`, which runs the scorer in a daemon thread named `MlflowScorer-<name>` that re-enters `run()` guarded by the `_in_scorer_timeout` ContextVar, then joins with `min(timeout, threading.TIMEOUT_MAX)`.
Symptom: One hung LLM judge call blocked the entire evaluation with no way to bound it; after the fix an overrun raises `MlflowTimeoutError`, which the harness records as a `SCORER_ERROR` row while other scorers still produce metrics.
Constraints: The timeout is validated in `scorer` (non-negative finite number, bool rejected). Thread-local MLflow state (active run, active model) is not carried into the worker because `_run_with_timeout` uses `copy_context()`, which only copies ContextVars, so a bounded scorer may not see the caller's active run; this was raised in review and is not shown as resolved. Abandoned threads keep running after a timeout. Code that asserts the scorer runs on a `MlflowGenAIEvalScorer` thread must not assume that name once a timeout applies.
applies: Custom scorers created with `mlflow.genai.scorers.scorer` (and anything that calls `Scorer.run`) in evaluate and monitoring; not for built-in judges that bypass `Scorer.run`.
says: A slow custom evaluation metric freezes the entire model assessment job indefinitely.
Timed out evaluation judges show up as scoring error entries in test results.
Allow setting a custom time limit for individual evaluation metrics.
Provide an option to disable the five minute timeout on long running judges.
Ensure stalled scoring checks do not prevent the remaining evaluation metrics from completing.
search: Custom GenAI scorer execution in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.run bounds invocations using a daemon thread with DEFAULT_SCORER_TIMEOUT (300s) by default, while timeout=0 disables it. Overruns raise MlflowTimeoutError recorded as SCORER_ERROR rows, while abandoned threads continue running. The runner copies ContextVars via copy_context() rather than thread-local MLflow state, applies to @scorer in evaluate and monitoring, and does not cover built-in judges bypassing Scorer.run.
